name: GridPatch Infrastructure Maintenance Full Kit
description: The working uniform of GLMZ's grid maintenance crews — the people who patch cracked conduit, reroute power lines after acid-rain shorts, and descend into junction crawlspaces that haven't been opened since the last generation of workers sealed them. It's a full-coverage kit designed for confined spaces, electrical hazard, and extended outdoor exposure. The outer shell is a hi-vis safety orange rain-resistant work jacket with a mesh lining, zippered chest pockets, and two forearm pockets designed to hold diagnostic tablets or cable tools. The back carries a large reflective GLMZ Infrastructure Services logo in silver-grey. Underneath is a charcoal flame-resistant work shirt, loose enough to move in, with a full-length arm channel on the left sleeve for accommodating chrome arm hardware — the channel secured with industrial velcro tabs that allow field-quick reconfiguration. Insulated navy work trousers with double-knee panels, an integrated tool belt loop system at the waist (six loops, three D-rings), and lower-leg cinch straps for tucking into boot tops. Boots are tall-shaft rubber-composite safety boots, knee-height, rated for standing water and mild chemical exposure — standard for street-level infrastructure work after rain events. A white hard hat with a brim-mounted LED strip sits on the head, the interior fitted with a foam impact liner. Safety glasses with side shields are pushed up onto the hard hat brim when not in use. A hi-vis vest goes over everything when working street-adjacent, doubling the reflective surface area.
functionality: Electrical and flame hazard resistance, full rain shell protection, chrome arm accommodation channel with velcro tabs, tool loop and D-ring belt system, lower-leg cinch straps for boot-tucking in standing water, brim-mounted LED strip for low-light confined work, hi-vis vest overlay for street-adjacent visibility compliance, chemical-resistant boot shaft.
what_it_says: City infrastructure. The people who keep the lights on and the conduit from flooding. The GLMZ Infrastructure Services logo means they're municipal-adjacent — not a corponation employee, but contracted through one, with just enough institutional backing to get into access hatches that most people never know exist. The worn boot shafts and the replacement foam in the hard hat mean this isn't new work.
manufacturer: GLMZ Infrastructure Services (jacket and hard hat issued; shirt and trousers from Ironpass Workwear contract; boots from Kessler Safety line)
price_range: Φ220–Φ310 (partially city-contracted subsidy; workers cover boot and underlayer costs)
story_hooks: A maintenance worker's access log shows they descended into a junction crawlspace beneath Circuit Block 7 four times last month — but there are no work orders for that block, and the conduit there was certified intact two years ago.

The LED strip on a hard hat has been modified to pulse in a specific pattern when powered on — a subtle signal, invisible to anyone who doesn't know what they're looking for, used to mark safe passage for someone moving through the tunnels below.

A grid maintenance crew was sent to a power short in a sealed sub-level and never filed a completion report. Their jackets were found neatly folded outside the access hatch. The hatch was sealed from the inside.

physical_description.visual_profile: A complete hi-vis infrastructure worker ensemble in safety orange and charcoal, designed for durability and visibility in confined urban utility spaces. The silhouette is utilitarian and blocky—broad-shouldered jacket over a loose work shirt, reinforced trousers with visible cargo loops, and tall protective boots. The overall impression is industrial, functional, and deliberately visible: a person built to be seen in dangerous spaces.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and oversized through the torso for movement and layering; reinforced at stress points (knees, elbows). Trousers sit at the natural waist with structural tool-belt integration. Sleeves are cut long and feature a dedicated left-side channel with velcro accommodation for cybernetic arms. Boots are tight at the ankle, looser through the calf for tucking trouser legs.
physical_description.primary_material: Safety orange rain-resistant ballistic weave jacket shell with mesh lining; charcoal flame-resistant treated cotton work shirt; navy double-weight canvas trousers with reinforced panels; tall knee-height rubber-composite safety boots with chemical-resistant coating.
physical_description.texture: Rough, industrial weave throughout. The jacket has a slick rain-resistant outer surface contrasting with soft mesh interior. Trousers show visible stitching and double-seam construction. Boot material is smooth rubber with subtle grip-tread texturing. Velcro strips on the sleeve are soft-touch industrial grade.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: safety orange jacket with silver-grey reflective GLMZ logo on back. Secondary: charcoal work shirt, navy trousers. Accent: white hard hat with integrated LED strip (cool white glow when active), silver-grey reflective striping throughout, black safety glasses with amber-tinted lenses.
physical_description.closures: Full-length heavy-duty zipper on jacket front; magnetic snaps on chest pockets for quick access; industrial velcro tabs on left sleeve for augmentation channel; cargo pocket zip closures; trouser waist has integrated webbing loops; boot laces are reflective paracord; hard hat has ratchet-fit interior liner.
distinctive_features: Large reflective GLMZ Infrastructure Services logo across entire back panel
Mesh-lined jacket for ventilation in confined spaces
Dedicated left-sleeve augmentation channel with velcro reconfiguration tabs
Six cargo loops and three D-rings integrated into waist for tool-belt attachment
Brim-mounted LED strip on hard hat (white diode, field-replaceable)
Lower-leg cinch straps for secure boot tuck
Foam impact liner inside hard hat
Chemical-resistant rubber boot coating rated for standing water and mild acid exposure
Side-shield safety glasses stored on hard hat brim
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. Standard-issue working-class infrastructure uniform. GLMZ is a mid-tier contractor corp; the kit signals essential service labor rather than disposable gig work.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this outfit identifies the person as licensed infrastructure crew—someone authorized to access grid junction spaces, conduit networks, and post-acid-rain utility damage zones. The visible augmentation accommodation signals normalized chrome hardware in this workforce. The high visibility is both practical and social: grid workers are essential and visibly essential to the GLMZ power grid.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. The jacket shows field wear—small acid-rain stains on the sleeves, scuffed reflective panels from crawlspace contact, but no tears. The trousers are clean but show fading at the knees from repeated kneeling. The hard hat has minor impact dents. Boots are scuffed but waterproofed and functional. This is a uniform that sees daily use and regular maintenance.
